segments.html: globals

Process-wide caches shared by every Tracer.

Tracing a with block means finding its source, parsing it to an AST, and compiling the block body — work that is identical every time the same block is entered. These two module-level dicts memoize that work across all tracer instances so, e.g., a with model.trace(...) inside a Python loop is read, parsed, and compiled exactly once.

Both grow with the number of distinct source files and trace sites seen during the process, which is bounded by the program's own source, so they are never evicted. Neither is re-validated against on-disk changes: a source edited mid-run is still traced as it was first seen (see Tracer.source). A process that builds blocks it receives — a server — runs other programs' source, so it confines each build to itself with block_scope.

segments.html: block_scope

Undo, on exit, what building a received block added to these caches and linecache.

RequestModel.deserialize registers a block's source in linecache under the client's filename, and the invokes inside it are parsed from there and memoized here under that filename. Kept, a later request from the same file is parsed against its predecessor's block — running the old invoke body, or finding no with at its line — and on a long-lived server all three grow with every client file seen.

The restore undoes whatever else registered meanwhile, so builds under it must not interleave.
